extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, corporate legal and finance teams, investors, and compliance professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-rule requirements for disclosing climate-related targets/goals, use of offsets/RECs, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions (Scopes 1–3), including what items must be disclosed when material and how progress, expenditures, and methodologies should be described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality threshold for targets and goals disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant must disclose any climate-related target or goal if such target or goal has materially affected or is reasonably likely to materially affect the registrant's business, results of operations, or financial condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule conditions disclosure on materiality to focus on decision-useful information; the Commission declined proposals to limit disclosure to only publicly announced targets or to those formally adopted by the board/CEO. Registrants are not required to disclose non-material internal targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of activities included in a disclosed target
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosing a material target or goal, include a description of the scope of activities included in the target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a non-exclusive example of information to disclose if necessary to understand the material impact; the final rule removed the explicit word 'emissions' from the items list—if a target is to reduce emissions, the scope should cover emissions as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of measurement for the target
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the unit of measurement used for the target or goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule eliminated a required item asking whether a target is absolute or intensity-based because unit of measurement disclosure will generally provide that information; units should be provided when necessary to understand the material impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined time horizon for achieving the target
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the defined time horizon by which the target is intended to be achieved, and whether that time horizon is based on one or more goals established by a climate-related treaty, law, regulation, policy, or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a non-exclusive example to be provided if necessary to understanding material impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline time period and means to track progress
rubrics_metrics.description: If a baseline has been established for the target, disclose the defined baseline time period and the means by which progress will be tracked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide this information when necessary to understand the material impact or reasonably likely material impact of the target; registrants should explain how progress will be measured against the baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative description of how the registrant intends to meet targets or goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a qualitative description of the registrant's intended approach to meet its climate-related target(s) or goal(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule specifies this discussion need only be qualitative to avoid excessive detail; registrants determine what specific factors to highlight. The Commission eliminated the proposed illustrative list (energy efficiency, offsets, carbon removal, etc.) so those are not required items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of progress toward meeting targets or goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose any progress toward meeting the target or goal and how such progress has been achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must update this disclosure each fiscal year describing actions taken during the year to achieve targets or goals; there is a phase-in for compliance with certain update requirements based on filer status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual updating requirement for targets and goals progress
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must update the targets/goals progress disclosure in each fiscal year following initial compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The update requirement aligns with transition plan update rules and enables investors to monitor impacts as registrants attempt to meet targets; phase-in timing parallels Subpart 1500 compliance schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative and qualitative disclosure of material expenditures and financial impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss any material impacts to the registrant's business, results of operations, or financial condition as a direct result of the target or goal or actions taken to make progress toward the target, including quantitative and qualitative disclosure of any material expenditures and material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should disclose material expenditures (operating and capital) and impacts on estimates/assumptions when those impacts are material; disclosure may cross-reference Rule 14-02(h) of Regulation S-X where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to explain expenditures and attribution qualitatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants have flexibility to explain qualitatively the nature of any disclosed expenditure and how it is a direct result of progress under a disclosed target or goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given challenges in disaggregating expenditures, registrants may explain attribution qualitatively and should consider aggregate materiality (if overall expenditures related to progress are material in the aggregate, disclose appropriately).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration/placement flexibility for targets and goals disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may provide required targets and goals disclosure as part of the Item 1502 transition plan discussion or in risk management discussion pursuant to Item 1503.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flexibility is intended to reduce redundancy across Subpart 1500 disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim targets disclosure not required
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule does not require registrants to disclose any interim targets set by the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission concluded interim targets are not separately necessary because material interim targets will likely be included in the registrant's plan discussion of how it intends to achieve the overall target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offsets and RECs disclosure when used as a material component
rubrics_metrics.description: If carbon offsets or renewable energy certificates (RECs) have been used as a material component of a registrant's plan to achieve climate-related targets or goals, disclose specified information about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A materiality qualifier was added: disclosure about offsets/RECs is required only when they are a material component of the plan to achieve a disclosed target or goal; registrants must determine importance based on facts and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount represented by offsets or RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the amount of carbon avoidance, reduction, or removal represented by the offsets or the amount of generated renewable energy represented by RECs used as a material component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure should distinguish among avoidance, reduction, and removal where applicable to help investors assess role in meeting net-zero or other targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and source of offsets or RECs (including type and market)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the nature and source of offsets or RECs, including whether an offset represents avoidance, reduction, or removal and whether an REC is bundled or unbundled and whether it was obtained from a compliance market or voluntary market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps investors evaluate quality, permanence, and market-related risks; Commission added 'nature' and 'source' to clarify differences among offset types and REC forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description and location of underlying offset/REC projects and authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a description and location of underlying projects and any registries or other authentication of the offsets or RECs used materially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about project location/project type and authentication helps investors assess legitimacy, standards compliance, and related risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of offsets or RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the cost of offsets or RECs if they are a material component of the registrant's plan to achieve targets or goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost disclosure aids investors in assessing financial impacts and risks tied to reliance on such instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of offsets/RECs role and related material risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether reliance on offsets/RECs as a material component of the plan introduces additional material risks (e.g., price volatility, supply constraints, reputational or litigation risk) that should be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants relying materially on offsets/RECs should consider disclosing related transition risks and implications for their business/financial condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose their Scope 1 (direct) and Scope 2 (indirect from purchased energy) GHG emissions for the most recently completed fiscal year and for historical fiscal years included in consolidated financial statements, to the extent reasonably available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement is based on GHG Protocol concepts to elicit consistent and comparable metrics; disclosure should be aligned with investors' need to assess transition risk exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 3 GHG emissions disclosure threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants (other than SRCs) must disclose Scope 3 emissions if those emissions are material or if the registrant has set a GHG emissions reduction target or goal that includes Scope 3 emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission recognized higher data-collection difficulty for Scope 3 and limited disclosure to material Scope 3 or Scope 3 included in targets to balance usefulness and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG disaggregation and units (constituent gases and CO2e) and gross terms
rubrics_metrics.description: For each of Scopes 1, 2, and 3 (as required), disclose emissions disaggregated by each constituent greenhouse gas and in the aggregate expressed in terms of CO2-equivalent, and disclose gross emissions excluding any purchased or generated offsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disaggregation allows investors to assess relative risks by constituent gas; gross terms exclude offsets to show actual emissions before any offsetting instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG intensity disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose GHG emissions in terms of intensity metrics where applicable (e.g., emissions per unit of output).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rules included intensity reporting alongside gross metrics to give investors relative performance information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology, significant inputs, and significant assumptions for GHG calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the methodology, significant inputs, and significant assumptions used to calculate GHG emissions metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where reasonable estimates are used, registrants must describe assumptions and reasons for estimates; this disclosure supports transparency and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational boundary alignment with consolidated financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Set organizational boundaries for GHG emissions disclosure using the same scope of entities, operations, assets, and other holdings as those included in the registrant's consolidated financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alignment is intended to provide investors a consistent view across financial and GHG disclosures; the same boundary approach applies to Scopes 1, 2, and 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reasonable estimates and Q4 estimate accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may use reasonable estimates when disclosing GHG emissions if actual measurement is not possible, and may use a reasonable estimate for the fourth fiscal quarter if actual reported data is not reasonably available, provided they disclose assumptions and later correct any material differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission encourages as accurate a measurement as reasonably possible but allows estimates with required explanation; if an estimated Q4 is used, registrant must promptly disclose any material difference between estimate and later-determined actual data.
